subject: Azure private offer — minimum usage safeguard and partner margin clarification
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Susan Kim <susan@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-17T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure private offer — draft and two asks

Hi Susan — thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is the draft private offer for CloudWave (Redwood_Azure_PO_Draft_v2.pdf). Two quick asks from our side before we lock numbers: 

1) Minimum-usage safeguard: you mentioned concern about committing to a strict monthly floor during the first quarter. We can propose a 3-month ramp (60%/80%/100% of committed runrate) instead of a full floor in month one — would that address your procurement constraints?

2) Channel margin and pass-through: we included a 14% reseller uplift in the draft. Please confirm whether your downstream contractors require a higher pass-through or if 14% is acceptable. If not, give us target % and we’ll run an ops workback.

Next steps: if those two items are fine, we’ll generate the formal DocuSign link and route to finance. If you want a firm example P&L for the margin carveout I can loop Ben to produce a quick workback.

Thanks — Aisha

--
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0127
From: Susan Kim <susan@cloudwave.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-17T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — draft and two asks

Aisha — thanks for the draft and the quick follow. A few responses inline: 

On the minimum-usage safeguard: the 3-month ramp sounds reasonable. Can we make the ramp opt-out at month 2 if actual usage is <50% of the ramped commitment? Finance wants a safety valve so we don't pay ahead if adoption is delayed.

On channel margin: our partners typically need 18% to maintain prevailing margin in the region; 14% will squeeze them too much. If Redwood can do 17% with a small marketing co-fund, we can close this quarter.

Also: finance asked whether you can split the commitment across two SKUs (core inference + extended-support addon) so they can capitalise differently.

I’ve CC’d finance for visibility.

—Susan
VP, Strategic Partnerships
CloudWave Analytics
susan@cloudwave.com
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-18T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Azure private offer — draft and two asks

Ben / Vanessa — forwarding Susan's ask. Key asks from CloudWave: 1) Add an opt-out safety valve at month 2 if usage <50% of ramp. 2) Increase partner pass-through to 17% (they asked for 18%, asked us to meet at 17% + marketing co-fund). 3) Split the commitment across two SKUs.

My read: the ramp opt-out is low-risk operationally but we need ops/legal language for the opt-out window. The pass-through bump is the main cost impact — see attached channel_margin_workback.xlsx for a quick sensitivity. Can we consider a conditional concession: 17% partner uplift in month 1-6 if CloudWave signs to a 9-month commit (instead of 12), otherwise revert to 14%? That shortens Redwood's exposure while giving them better near-term economics. Also we could offer a $25k marketing co-fund spread over Q3.

Can you run numbers and confirm if the conditional 17% + 9-month term + $25k co-fund is approvable? If yes I’ll draft updated terms and the SKU split proposal for finance.

Thanks — Aisha

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-18T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Azure private offer — draft and two asks

Adding final approval and ops note. Short answers: 

1) Ramp opt-out: approved. Legal to add clause: 30-day usage review at end of month 2 with opt-out if <50% realized usage. Ops will need telemetry gating; SLA unchanged.

2) Channel uplift: we can do conditional 17% for months 1–6 if CloudWave signs a 9-month committed term (instead of 12) and accepts a $25k marketing co-fund (payable across Q3). Finance ran quick P&L and the 17% hit is manageable under that structure (see channel_margin_workback.xlsx).

3) SKU split: approved. Product ops to create separate SKU for core inference + 'enterprise support' addon; pricing team will map billing codes to allow capitalisation.

Please update the PO draft with the conditional language and confirm when you plan to send the DocuSign. Recommend we also add an ops acceptance checklist in the DocuSign (telemetry gate, billing account mapping).

Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Deals — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: channel_margin_workback.xlsx (detailed scenarios).
